vacancies.title: Antenna Engineer
vacancies.assessment: Starion's official live vacancy overview now lists application deadline 2 November 2026, extended from the previously stored 26 October; individual job detail page still lists 26 October (conflicting official dates). Confirm the later deadline with recruiter. Direct ESTEC RF Payloads role, but six years of specialised antenna/RF experience required and substantial mechanical-engineering domain mismatch.

vacancies.title: MBSE Engineer
vacancies.location: Leiden, Netherlands (Dutch Ministry of Defence naval programme; not ESTEC)
vacancies.assessment: Official Starion vacancy page and job overview now give a 16 November 2026 application deadline (extended from 2 November). Leiden-based Dutch Ministry of Defence naval programme, not direct ESA/ESTEC. Requires at least three years hands-on MBSE, Capella and maritime/naval experience; specialist domain and tool gap remains.

vacancies.title: Post Launch Engineer
vacancies.assessment: Direct ESTEC post-launch engineering and technical coordination across satellite operations, anomaly investigations, industrial contractors and system reviews. Relevant broad engineering coordination and ESA exposure, but 10 years satellite operations/spacecraft development plus 3 years satellite systems coordination are major specialist seniority gaps. Stretch role; salary unknown.

vacancies.title: SatCom Payload Engineer
vacancies.location: Noordwijk, Netherlands / Harwell, United Kingdom (listed options; detailed description emphasises ESA ECSAT Harwell; confirm Dutch placement)
vacancies.assessment: Official listing includes Noordwijk as well as Harwell, but role narrative says ESA ECSAT in Harwell; verify actual ESTEC work location before applying. Four years aerospace/satcom equipment experience and specialist satellite payload architecture expertise requested. Some hardware/manufacturing overlap, but satellite communications specialization is a large mismatch. Salary unknown.
